newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's BNDES allowed to finance forex contracts.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's BNDES allowed to finance forex contracts.

text.p: Brazil's Central Bank on Wednesday allowed the National Development Bank (BNDES) to finance exporters' foreign exchange contracts (ACC), an official said.
Jose Maria Ferreira Carvalho, head of the Central Bank's foreign exchange department, said exporters would be allowed to take out Finamex credit in addition to ACCs, with banks to finance exports.
They could also use the BNDES finance to pay off foreign exchange contracts, he told reporters.
Carvalho said the Finamex finance could have a maturity of between 8-10 years.
"The objective is to give the exporter longer financing terms," he said.

The government has recently taken steps to boost exports and counter a burgeoning trade deficit, which reached $2.9 billion in the first 10 months of the year and is expected by analysts to expand to at least $4.0 billion by the year-end.
